checks.note: reconfirm's guard is time-only (uploadConfirmedAt within uploadTtlSeconds), so a within-window replay of an older key does republish StorageObjectConfirmedEvent — the trigger is real in this file — but the claimed consequence depends on CoachProfilePhotoEventListener.onStorageConfirmed/updatePhotoUrlByUserId (whether it overwrites unconditionally) and on deletePhoto's transaction/locking, neither shown here; the deployed uploadTtlSeconds value (claimed 600s) is also in config not shown.

confirmUpload validates only head.contentType, head.contentLength and eTag non-blankness; persistConfirmed stores request.checksum() verbatim and toConfirmUploadResponse/findActiveObject surface it via formatChecksum as "sha256:<hex>", with signUpload's presigned PUT binding only contentType (no x-amz-checksum). The verification caveat (ReplicatedStorageService/outbox handlers) is moot for the surfaced claim: ConfirmUploadResponse returns the unverified value before any outbox job runs, and replication is conditionally enabled anyway.

The file confirms saveStep2/saveStep3 do deleteByCoachId+flush+saveAll with only an unlocked requireProfile, while saveStep1/saveStep4/deletePhoto/publishProfile all take findByIdForUpdate — the asymmetry is real. But the finding's own verification caveat (no controller-level per-user serialization in front of the profile-builder endpoints) cannot be checked: only this service file was provided, so the controller/filter layer is missing.

The trigger is real in this file: deletePhoto's catch (AuthorizationException) block falls through to profile.setPhotoUrl(null) + save, and the post-refresh null-check makes retries no-ops, so the FSO row is orphaned without soft-deletion. But the consequence (permanent quota leak, replay eligibility) depends on FileStorageService.softDelete's throw ordering, sumSizeBytesByOwnerId, and the finding's own required sweeper check in the filestorage module — none of that code is available here, so the verification caveat cannot be run.

confirmUpload does publish StorageObjectConfirmedEvent in-memory after transactionTemplate.execute commits (outbox is used only for replication in persistConfirmed), and reconfirm re-publishes only within uploadTtlSeconds — the mechanism is as described. But the finding's permanence claim hinges on its verification caveat (no reconciliation job re-linking coach_profile FSOs outside the event path), which lives in code outside this file and is not shown.

matches.note: R1 points at confirmUpload's HEAD-only validation and the consequence of serving unvalidated content, but its mechanism is re-PUT swap after confirm, not that declared content type is never checked against the actual bytes.
No reported finding mentions that a rejected confirm leaves the already-PUT object in the bucket uncounted and uncleaned.
R4 cites application/octet-stream and .bin in the global allow-list but only as an enabler of the photo-path issue, not as a defect defeating the allow-list itself.
No reported finding covers signUpload accepting arbitrary entity strings with ownership checked only for OWNER_BOUND_ENTITIES.

R4 states saveStep5 checks only the string prefix and never verifies a confirmed, owned, non-deleted image object, with the same consequence of a non-image or nonexistent key becoming the public photo.
